vo: In July 2018, one line buried in a nearly two-hundred-page annual report caused a global scandal.
vis: a thick corporate annual report lying open on a dark desk under a lamp, one line underlined in red ink, London skyline faintly through rain-streaked window, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: It said Burberry had destroyed twenty-eight point six million pounds' worth of its own products. In one year.
vis: a pile of luxury beige trench coats and handbags stacked on a pallet inside a dark industrial facility, dramatic top light, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: Trench coats. Handbags. Perfume. Never worn. Never sold. Burned.
vis: brand-new luxury trench coat and perfume bottles being consumed by flames inside an industrial incinerator, orange glow, sparks, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: And the company wasn't hiding it. It had been writing it down, year after year.
vis: stack of old annual reports on a shelf in a dim archive, dust in lamp light, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: Because destroying perfectly good products isn't a mistake. It's a business model.
vis: a luxury store window at night, elegant mannequin in a trench coat, reflection of flames in the glass, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: This is the story of everything that was never supposed to be sold.
vis: dark cork board covered in photos of luxury goods, red strings, case files, an incinerator photo in the center, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: Here's what the report actually said: the cost of finished goods physically destroyed in the year was twenty-eight point six million pounds.
vis: close-up of a printed financial report page with numbers, a magnifying glass resting on it, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: That included ten point four million pounds of beauty products, which the company linked to a new licence deal with Coty.
vis: rows of luxury perfume bottles on a dark shelf, some knocked over, cold blue light, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: The year before, the figure was twenty-six point nine million. The year before that, eighteen point eight million.
vis: old ledger book with handwritten columns of numbers, fountain pen, desk lamp, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: Over five years, more than ninety million pounds of the company's own products went up in smoke.
vis: thick black smoke rising from an industrial chimney at dusk over a grey city, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: Shareholders were furious. At the annual meeting, one investor asked why they couldn't simply buy the leftover stock.
vis: a corporate shareholder meeting in a dark wood-paneled hall, silhouettes of people in rows, one person standing with raised hand, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: The company's answer: the energy from burning was captured, and it only destroyed items carrying its trademark.
vis: industrial waste-to-energy plant at night with glowing furnace windows and steam, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: But that last detail is the real clue.
vis: extreme close-up of a luxury brand label sewn into a beige coat, no readable text, shallow depth of field, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: Luxury doesn't sell a product. It sells scarcity.
vis: a single luxury handbag alone on a pedestal in a vast dark empty boutique, spotlight, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: A trench coat that costs well over a thousand pounds in a flagship store only works if you can't find it for a fraction of that somewhere else.
vis: elegant flagship luxury boutique interior, warm light, a beige trench coat displayed on a mannequin, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: Every discounted piece on a market stall or a grey-market website quietly tells customers: this brand isn't special.
vis: cluttered street market stall at night with piles of discounted designer-looking bags and coats under harsh bulbs, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: And unsold stock is a risk. It can be stolen, leaked, copied, or sold on cheaply.
vis: shadowy figure in a warehouse loading boxes into an unmarked van at night, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: So for decades, the cleanest solution was fire.
vis: a match being struck in darkness, flame lighting a pile of folded designer clothes, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: And Burberry wasn't alone.
vis: dark cork board with polaroids of luxury watches, perfume and handbags connected with red string, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: Richemont, the group behind Cartier, bought back unsold watches from its own retailers.
vis: luxury watch display case in a jewellery store being emptied by gloved hands, watches placed into a black box, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: Around four hundred and eighty million euros' worth in two years. Many were dismantled and recycled for parts.
vis: watchmaker's workbench with a luxury watch disassembled into tiny gears and parts, loupe, warm lamp, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: The reason, as the company put it: watches sitting in the grey market don't help long-term brand value.
vis: dim back-alley shop window displaying discounted luxury watches with handwritten price cards, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: In other words: it's better to destroy a product than to let it be sold cheaply.
vis: a luxury watch lying on an anvil next to a heavy hammer, dramatic side light, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: But there's a second reason. And it's hidden in tax law.
vis: dusty law books and customs forms on a desk, stamp and ink pad, lamp light, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: In the United States, a rule called duty drawback lets importers claim back up to ninety-nine percent of the import duties they paid.
vis: a busy container port at dusk, stacks of shipping containers, cranes, customs office in foreground, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: The condition: the goods have to be exported again, or destroyed under customs supervision.
vis: customs officer with clipboard watching boxes of clothing being fed into an industrial shredder, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: So an unsold shirt that just sits in a warehouse costs money. A destroyed one can bring money back.
vis: split lighting: a dusty warehouse shelf of boxed shirts on one side, a stack of cash on the other, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: And storage isn't free. Every week a product sits on a shelf, someone is paying rent for it.
vis: endless aisles of a giant fulfilment warehouse with tall shelves, cold fluorescent light, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: In 2021, an undercover investigation inside one Amazon warehouse in Scotland showed what that math looks like.
vis: hidden camera style shot inside a huge fulfilment center at night, grainy, workers far away, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: Smart TVs, laptops, headphones, sealed face masks, sorted into boxes marked destroy.
vis: cardboard boxes overflowing with new boxed electronics, headphones and face masks, a red stamp-like DESTROY label shape without text, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: A former worker said the weekly target was around one hundred and thirty thousand items. One leaked week showed one hundred and twenty-four thousand marked destroy, and twenty-eight thousand marked donate.
vis: a leaked spreadsheet on a laptop screen in a dark room, numbers blurred, glow on a person's hands, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: Amazon denied sending the goods to landfill. But the footage had already gone around the world.
vis: news broadcast monitors in a dark control room all showing warehouse footage, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: Then online shopping made the problem explode.
vis: mountain of cardboard delivery parcels piled up in a dark room, dramatic top light, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: In 2024, Americans returned an estimated eight hundred and ninety billion dollars' worth of goods.
vis: huge returns processing center with conveyor belts carrying opened parcels and clothes, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: That's almost seventeen percent of everything retailers sold.
vis: aerial view of a giant parking lot of delivery trucks at a distribution center at night, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: Many shoppers now buy two sizes and send one back. More than half of Gen Z shoppers say they've done it.
vis: young person at home surrounded by opened shopping bags and two identical sneaker boxes, phone in hand, moody light, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: But a returned item has to be checked, cleaned, repackaged and restocked. And that often costs more than the item is worth.
vis: warehouse worker inspecting a returned sweater at a sorting table under harsh light, piles of returns, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: So it goes somewhere else: to off-price stores, to liquidators, to tightly packed bales shipped overseas, or straight to the incinerator.
vis: giant compressed bales of mixed clothing stacked in a port warehouse ready for shipping, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: One estimate says returns in the US created eight point four billion pounds of landfill waste in a single year.
vis: enormous landfill with clothes and cardboard, gulls, grey sky, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: A huge share of those bales ends up in one place: Kantamanto market in Accra, Ghana.
vis: vast crowded secondhand clothing market in Accra with tarps and piles of clothes, traders, documentary photo, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: Around fifteen million used garments arrive there every week.
vis: workers unloading huge bales of secondhand clothes from a truck at a market, dust in sunlight, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: According to the Or Foundation, about forty percent of each bale can't be sold and leaves the market as waste.
vis: trader cutting open a bale of clothes and sorting unsellable stained garments into a pile, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: Some of it is burned. Some of it washes onto Accra's beaches, in tangled ropes of fabric.
vis: beach in West Africa covered in tangled ropes of discarded clothing, waves, overcast sky, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: The clothes the West didn't want to burn at home are often burned anyway. Just further away.
vis: smoke rising from burning textile waste near a city at dusk, silhouettes, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: In September 2018, just two months after the scandal, Burberry announced it would stop destroying unsold products, with immediate effect.
vis: press conference podium with microphones in a dark elegant room, camera flashes, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: France went further. In 2022, it became the first country to ban the destruction of unsold non-food goods.
vis: Paris government building at night, French flag, rain on cobblestones, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: And on the nineteenth of July 2026, the European Union followed: large companies can no longer destroy unsold clothes, accessories or shoes.
vis: European Parliament hemicycle in Brussels, dramatic wide shot, warm light, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: Even recycling an unsold item now counts as destruction, unless a narrow exception applies.
vis: recycling plant with shredded textile fibres on a conveyor belt, industrial light, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: Medium-sized companies follow in 2030.
vis: calendar on a desk turned to the year 2030, pen and documents, lamp light, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: Here's the uncomfortable part. Brands aren't wrong that discounts can hurt them.
vis: luxury boutique with a single SALE rack in the corner, empty and dim, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: And not every destroyed item is a scandal. Unsafe, damaged or counterfeit goods sometimes have to go.
vis: counterfeit handbags seized and piled on a customs table, officers' gloved hands, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: But a ban doesn't make overproduction disappear. It just forces companies to find another exit: resale, donation, outlets, or simply making less.
vis: factory floor with sewing machines and rows of identical garments being produced, cold light, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: So the next time you see a luxury price tag, remember what it's protecting.
vis: close-up of a blank luxury price tag hanging from a designer coat, dark background, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: Not just the product. The idea that it will never be cheap.
vis: a luxury handbag behind thick glass in a museum-like display, spotlight, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: For years, the price of that idea was a fire nobody was supposed to see.
vis: glowing embers and ash of burned fabric in darkness, a single unburned label, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9

vo: Would you rather a brand burn its leftovers, or sell them at a discount? Tell me in the comments.
vis: dark cork board with case photos, red strings, a closed case file stamped on the desk, lamp light, dark investigative documentary still, cinematic, photorealistic, moody warm lamp light, film grain, no text, no logos, 16:9
